task: Remove an arbitrary object-method name special case from raising-call Rust lowering.
observation: NativeGenerator treated any method named `poke` as a raising method in both function classification and call lowering, even when checked method metadata was available. A locally defined raising Box.poke therefore went through a different error bridge from an equivalent metadata-resolved raising method. Removing the name checks makes the checked metadata path emit ordinary `?` propagation; a focused regression verifies that output.
impact: A user-defined method name could alter code generation independently of its checked raise effects. This correction removes that fixture-specific behavior for this path; general Rust backend validity still requires the frozen-candidate native acceptance gate.
evidence: scripts/java/test.sh (all 12 test classes passed under ABI-v9)

resolution.summary: The exercised local raising method now follows checked method metadata. Broader Rust codegen correctness remains open.

task: Preserve an escaping raise after a completed local recovery in generated function signatures.
observation: A function with a handled raise inside try/recover followed by a top-level raise was accepted by both checkers. C++ generated a Result-returning function, but Java generated a plain i64 function and lowered the later raise to abort. The Java raising-function scan used one function-wide hasTry flag, so an earlier try incorrectly hid later top-level raises. Since nested try statements contain their own raises, every top-level Raise can independently classify its function as raising.
impact: This generated invalid Rust for a semantically valid function that propagates a failure after a recovery block. Java now emits the Result carrier, matching C++ for the reduced case; native compilation remains deferred.
evidence: scripts/java/test.sh and MOSS_STAGED_ABI=v10 scripts/java/test.sh (12 test classes each passed)

resolution.summary: Top-level escaping raises now classify the function independently of earlier recovery blocks; the focused generated signature assertion passes.

task: Lower a statically routed domain whose source declaration has per-instance inferred layouts.
observation: Both C++ and Java accepted tests/specialized_domain_routes.moss. C++ generated a closed WorkerHandle that carries base and inferred-specialization refs, but Java generated the Coordinator route fields as WorkerRef while also generating a distinct Worker__w2Ref. The source-level accepted route therefore had no matching Java backend type. Java now records specialization source identity and emits a closed nominal handle, converts constructor route arguments into it, and dispatches handlers whose signatures agree across all variants.
impact: The prior Java output could not represent accepted statically routed instances with different inferred layouts. The focused regression verifies generated type relationships and dispatch, but Rust compilation and native behavior remain unverified until the final candidate gate.
evidence: scripts/java/test.sh and MOSS_STAGED_ABI=v10 scripts/java/test.sh (12 test classes each passed)

resolution.summary: Java now emits the closed route handle and compatible root-call dispatch for the exercised base-plus-specialization topology; native validation remains deferred.
